title: 2525 cannot start route on selected icon update

issues.title: Can't start route on asset
issues.body:
I did think this issue was fixed - we needed PlanningForce to re-render if `interactive` changed.

But, we still can't start/end a route on some assets.  It may be because the asset is `selected`.  Note: if an asset is `selected` (flashing) or `current` part of the currently selected orders, then it doesn't get clustered, and is `raw`.

When an asset is `clustered`, we can select it.  It's just that we can't when they are `raw`.  We do have the concept of `interactive` - to stop icons taking a click when we're route planning. But, this seems to work for `clustered` assets, and not `raw` assets.

The two different types of assets are created in slightly different ways. Maybe there is another cause.

Note:  I've made a workaround for this, but it's a bit clumsy.    The issue is with markers that have not been clustered are not going "non-interactive" when we're planning orders.  From `PlanningForce` it looks like they should, but they remain interactive.    The workaround is to prevent `raw` (non-clustered) asset from ever being interactive. Sadly, this prevents users from clicking to un-select.

Steps to reproduce:
- zoom in on part of map
- select an asset - it will start to flash
- now go up and plan. set of orders (land-route is easy)
- try to start route on flashing asset.  We can't.  Similarly, we can't end a route on an asset

Aah, I think I've got it.  In React-Leaflet, they don't update the marker when `interactive` changes:
https://github.com/PaulLeCam/react-leaflet/blob/master/packages/react-leaflet/src/Marker.tsx

Have submitted [PR](https://github.com/PaulLeCam/react-leaflet/pull/1064).  I've now introduced a new workaround.  We force `React-leaflet` to ALWAYS create new raw markers  by modifying the `key` - by adding the current time-millis.  In this way the value of `interactive` gets used.

But, getting the react-leaflet solution in first is better.

**Update** I think this workaround is causing more screen updates.  An alternate workaround would be to cache the value of interactive and force a key update when the value of interactive updates.   We _Could_ use some kind of counter but toggling between two states may be enough.
